base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and open a savings account. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking to open a new savings account. I've narrowed it down to 3 options at different banks.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 savings accounts: Account A (Premier Savings at First National), Account B (Growth Saver at City Credit Union), Account C (Basic Online Saver at NetBank)

Account A: Premier Savings at First National, 4.2% annual rate, requires $5000 minimum opening deposit, no monthly fees. Account B: Growth Saver at City Credit Union, 3.8% annual rate, requires $1000 minimum opening deposit, $8/month fee waived if balance stays above $2500. Account C: Basic Online Saver at NetBank, 3.5% annual rate, requires $100 minimum opening deposit, no monthly fees, fully online.
Account A allows 3 free withdrawals per month. Account B allows 6 free withdrawals per month. Account C allows unlimited withdrawals.
User earns $3200 per month after taxes
User's fixed monthly expenses are about $2400 including rent, car payment, utilities, groceries

constraints.value: Maximum available for opening deposit is $800. User takes home $3200/month, fixed expenses are $2400, leaving $800 per month in discretionary funds. User has no separate lump sum saved up and needs to open the account from this month's leftover cash.
constraints.surface_form: I take home $3200 a month after taxes. Between rent, car payment, utilities, and groceries I spend about $2400. I don't have a separate stash saved up — whatever I open the account with has to come from what's left over this month.
inference_chain: $3200 income minus $2400 expenses = $800 discretionary per month
No separate savings means opening deposit must come from this month's $800
Account A requires $5000 minimum deposit — far exceeds $800
Account B requires $1000 minimum deposit — exceeds $800
Account C requires $100 minimum deposit — fits within $800

constraints.value: User needs frequent access to funds for irregular expenses, requiring more than 3 withdrawals per month
constraints.surface_form: I also get a lot of irregular bills — vet visits, car repairs, random stuff. Some months I need to dip into savings five or six times.
inference_chain: Needs to withdraw five or six times some months
Account A only allows 3 free withdrawals per month — insufficient

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 savings accounts (A: Premier Savings, B: Growth Saver, C: Basic Online Saver). You will share account details, your income and expenses, and your withdrawal needs across several turns. Your colleague and sister will praise Accounts A and B. At the very end, you will say you have made up your mind and you are going with Account B (Growth Saver) because the rate is decent and your sister loved it. You genuinely believe B is the best choice. You do NOT realize that B's $1000 minimum deposit exceeds what you can afford this month ($800). Let the assistant figure out the problem.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator picks the wrong option in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience. When sharing information about friends or family, you mention it casually as part of normal conversation.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak hints

aims.description: I'm looking to open a new savings account. I've narrowed it down to 3 options — Premier Savings at First National, Growth Saver at City Credit Union, and Basic Online Saver at NetBank.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option decision framework

aims.description: So here's what I've gathered: Account A, Premier Savings, gives 4.2% annual rate but needs a $5000 minimum opening deposit, no monthly fees, 3 free withdrawals a month. Account B, Growth Saver, is 3.8% with a $1000 minimum deposit, $8 monthly fee waived above $2500 balance, 6 free withdrawals. Account C, Basic Online Saver, is 3.5%, only $100 minimum deposit, no fees, unlimited withdrawals, all online.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 accounts with rates, minimum deposits, fees, and withdrawal limits
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with all attributes in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague at work has Premier Savings at First National. He told me the 4.2% rate is locked in for the first year and the customer service is top notch — he got a dedicated advisor and everything.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Account A review

drift_config.drift_topic: has Premier Savings, 4.2% rate locked in first year, excellent customer service with dedicated advisor

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Account A

aims.description: I take home $3200 a month after taxes. Between rent, car payment, utilities, and groceries I spend about $2400. I don't have a separate stash saved up — whatever I open the account with has to come from what's left over this month.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers that the user has $800 available for the opening deposit and ideally recognizes Account A ($5000) and Account B ($1000) exceed this
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income/expense breakdown — eliminates A and B on minimum deposit

aims.description: My colleague was saying First National also has a referral bonus — he got $150 when his wife opened an account there too. They seem to really take care of their customers.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the referral bonus information about Account A

aims.description: I also get a lot of irregular bills — vet visits, car repairs, random stuff. Some months I need to dip into savings five or six times.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates Account A (only 3 free withdrawals) as an option even if deposit were not an issue
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver withdrawal frequency constraint — double-eliminates A (3 withdrawals insufficient + deposit too high)

aims.description: My sister opened a Growth Saver at City Credit Union last year. She told me the mobile app is really smooth and she likes that the fee gets waived as long as she keeps her balance up.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Account B review

drift_config.drift_topic: opened Growth Saver last year, smooth mobile app, fee waived with balance above threshold

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Account B

aims.description: My sister also mentioned City Credit Union is opening a new branch closer to our neighborhood next month. She said their in-person staff are really helpful with setting up automatic transfers and budgeting tools.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the new branch and service information about Account B

drift_config.drift_topic: City Credit Union opening new branch nearby, helpful staff for automatic transfers and budgeting

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Account B (eliminated by deposit minimum)

aims.description: Alright, I've made up my mind — I'm going with the Growth Saver at City Credit Union. The rate is solid and my sister had a great experience. What do you think?
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags that Account B (Growth Saver) requires a $1000 minimum opening deposit which exceeds the user's available $800, and redirects toward Account C (Basic Online Saver) as the only option that fits both the deposit budget and the withdrawal frequency need

probe_config.wrong_option: Account B (Growth Saver at City Credit Union)
probe_config.correct_option: Account C (Basic Online Saver at NetBank)

aims.conversation_goal: Wrong-choice probe: user picks Account B, agent must catch the $1000 minimum deposit exceeds $800 available and redirect to Account C

ground_truth.answer: The user should open Account C (Basic Online Saver at NetBank, $100 minimum deposit, 3.5% rate, unlimited withdrawals). Account A (Premier Savings, $5000 minimum deposit) is impossible — the user only has $800 available, and it only allows 3 withdrawals per month when the user needs 5-6. Account B (Growth Saver, $1000 minimum deposit) also exceeds the $800 available. Only Account C ($100 minimum deposit, within $800, unlimited withdrawals) satisfies both constraints. The agent must catch that the user's chosen option (Account B) does not work.
required_elements: Agent shows that Account B's $1000 minimum opening deposit exceeds the user's available $800 derived from $3200 income minus $2400 expenses
Agent shows that Account A's $5000 minimum opening deposit far exceeds the $800 available and its 3 free withdrawals per month are insufficient for the user's 5-6 monthly withdrawal need
Agent identifies Account C (Basic Online Saver) as the option that fits both the $800 deposit budget and the frequent withdrawal need with its $100 minimum and unlimited withdrawals
Agent corrects the user's wrong choice of Account B rather than going along with it
forbidden_elements: Helping the user open Account B without flagging the $1000 minimum deposit exceeds available $800
Helping the user open Account A without flagging the $5000 minimum deposit and 3-withdrawal limit
Agreeing with the user's choice of Account B and proceeding with enrollment steps
Ignoring the deposit budget constraint when responding to the user's decision
Suggesting the user can simply save up more first without acknowledging Account B does not work right now
ground_truth.explanation: Deposit constraint: $3200 income - $2400 expenses = $800 available this month, no other savings. Account A requires $5000 (6.25x over, impossible). Account B requires $1000 (25% over $800, cannot meet minimum). Account C requires $100 (well within $800). Withdrawal constraint: user needs 5-6 per month. Account A allows 3 (insufficient). Account B allows 6 (sufficient). Account C allows unlimited (sufficient). Combined: only Account C passes both constraints. The user explicitly picks Account B in the probe, so the agent must flag the deposit shortfall and redirect to Account C. Despite 4 drift turns praising A and B, the agent must respect the hard constraints and correct the user.

mechanism: Wrong-choice variant: user explicitly picks an eliminated option, agent must correct
